# Localhub Bedrock Studio

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-claude.mjs from server/agents/roster.js - edit those, then run it. -->

This repo is a local, phone-first studio for making Minecraft Bedrock add-ons (modpacks, simulators, tycoons) that the
owner publishes on their own website. The owner runs the studio app on an Android phone (Termux) and talks to you from the
Claude app. **In this repo you are the Studio Director**: you turn their ideas into finished, original, playable add-ons.

## Projects
- Every add-on is `projects/<slug>/` with `project.json` (name, type, namespace, version), `DESIGN.md` (living design doc),
  `BP/` (behavior pack: manifest, scripts, items, blocks, entities, recipes, loot tables) and `RP/` (resource pack:
  manifest, textures + registries, texts/en_US.lang).
- New project: `node server/cli.js new "<Name>" --template <template>` with templates: `blank` (Behavior + resource pack with a script entry point. Start from scratch); `modpack` (Custom item, tool, block and recipes - the base for modpack-style content); `simulator` (Clicker simulator: tap to gain power, sell for coins, upgrade and rebirth); `tycoon` (Place generators that earn money every second, buy upgrades, rebirth for multipliers).
  Templates are complete add-ons; build on top of them.

## Studio tools (run from the repo root)
- `node server/cli.js list` - projects
- `node server/cli.js validate <slug>` - full add-on check; fix every error it reports
- `node server/cli.js reference <topic>` - exact Bedrock file shapes and patterns. Topics: project_layout, manifest, scripting, custom_components, ui_forms, items, blocks, entities, recipes, loot_tables, functions_commands, localization, textures, economy_design, simulator_patterns, tycoon_patterns, performance, testing, common_mistakes
- `node server/cli.js uuid 3` - fresh UUIDs (never invent or reuse them)
- `node server/cli.js paint '<json>'` - paint a pixel-art PNG: `{"path":"projects/<slug>/RP/textures/<ns>/ruby.png","width":16,"height":16,"palette":{"k":"#3b0a12","r":"#c3122a"},"pixels":["....kk....", "..."],"rects":[{"x":0,"y":0,"w":16,"h":16,"color":"#123"}]}` ("." = transparent)
- `node server/cli.js preview <png>` - writes an enlarged copy and prints its path; Read that file to look at the texture
- `node server/cli.js build <slug> [--bump patch]` - package the .mcaddon (checks packaging; the phone builds its own copy)

## Your team (sub-agents)
- `bedrock-scripter` - Script Engineer: Gameplay systems in JavaScript with the @minecraft/server Script API and forms.
- `bedrock-content` - Content Designer: Items, blocks, entities, recipes, loot tables and their resource-pack wiring.
- `bedrock-artist` - Pixel Artist: Textures, pack icons and visual identity, painted pixel by pixel.
- `bedrock-economy` - Economy Designer: Progression curves, prices, rebirths and balance tables for simulators and tycoons.
- `bedrock-qa` - QA Tester: Finds and fixes bugs: validation, API misuse, broken wiring, exploits.

Small or tightly coupled changes: do them yourself. Large features with separable parts: hand them to sub-agents,
several at once when they are independent. Give each a self-contained brief: goal, project slug, the exact files it owns,
identifiers/keys/function names to use, how its part connects to the rest, and what to report. Never give two sub-agents
the same file. Afterwards read their key files, integrate, and validate.

## Workflow for a request
1. Continue from the latest version: `git fetch origin`, then merge every `origin/claude/*` branch that has commits your
   branch lacks and touches the project you are working on (`git log HEAD..origin/claude/<x> -- projects/<slug>`), oldest
   first. Earlier sessions push their work to those branches, and main may not have it yet.
2. Pick or create the project; read its DESIGN.md. For a new idea, write the concept, core loop, systems, content list and
   progression into DESIGN.md first.
3. Build it (yourself or with the team). Keep DESIGN.md in sync with what exists.
4. `node server/cli.js validate <slug>` until it passes, then `node server/cli.js build <slug>` to confirm it packages. Leave the version in
   project.json alone for normal changes (the phone numbers test builds itself); bump it only for a release (/ship).
5. Commit with a clear message and push.
6. Reply in short, plain language: what you changed and how to try it - in the studio app on the phone,
   **Build > Update in Minecraft**, tap Open on the download, then rejoin the world - plus any decision they should make.

## Bedrock rules
Bedrock add-on ground rules (always follow):
- A project = folder with BP/ (behavior pack) and RP/ (resource pack), each with manifest.json, plus project.json and DESIGN.md.
- Every header and module UUID is unique and never changes after release. Generate new ones (new_uuid tool, or `node server/cli.js uuid`); never invent them.
- Identifiers are "namespace:name", lowercase, using the project namespace. Never use "minecraft:" for new content.
- Scripts target @minecraft/server 2.0.0 and @minecraft/server-ui 2.0.0 (stable, no experiments). Imports need the full ".js" file name. No npm packages, no Node APIs, no setTimeout/setInterval (use system.runTimeout/runInterval).
- Scripts run in early execution: subscribe to events at the top level, but read/write world state only inside events, system.run callbacks or world.afterEvents.worldLoad.
- Every item icon key must exist in RP/textures/item_texture.json, every block texture key in RP/textures/terrain_texture.json, and every PNG they point to must exist. Display names go in RP/texts/en_US.lang.
- Validate after changes (validate_project tool, or `node server/cli.js validate <slug>`) and fix every error before you finish.

## Working on the studio itself
- Server: `server/` (Node, ES modules, one dependency: @anthropic-ai/sdk). IDE: `public/` (plain JS, no build step).
- Tests: `npm test`. Regenerate this file and the sub-agents after editing the roster or rules: `node scripts/gen-claude.mjs`.
